Purpose PARADIGM-HF demonstrated the superiority of sacubitril/valsartan over enalapril in patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HF-REF). How widely applicable sacubitril/valsartan treatment is in unselected patients with HF-REF is not known. We examined eligibility of patients with HF-REF for treatment with sacubitril/valsartan, according to the criteria used in PARADIGM-HF, in the Swedish Heart Failure Registry (SwedeHF). Methods Patients were considered potentially eligible if they were not hospitalized, had symptoms (NYHA class II–IV) and a reduced LVEF (≤ 40%), and were prescribed an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEI) or angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB) at a dose equivalent to enalapril ≥ 10 mg daily. In these patients, we evaluated further eligibility according to the main additional PARADIGM-HF inclusion criteria. Results Of 12,866 outpatients in NYHA functional class II–IV with an LVEF ≤ 40%, 9577 were prescribed at least 10 mg of enalapril (or equivalent) daily. Complete additional data were available for 3099 of these patients (32.4%) and of them 75.5% were potentially eligible for treatment with sacubitril/valsartan. The most common reason for ineligibility was a low natriuretic peptide level ( n = 462, 14.9%). Only a small proportion of patients were ineligible due to low eGFR or serum potassium level. Because only 78% of patients were taking ≥ 10 mg enalapril or equivalent daily, only 58.9% of all patients (75.5% of 78%) were eligible for sacubitril/valsartan. Conclusions Between 34 and 76% of symptomatic patients with HF-REF in a ‘real world’ population are eligible for treatment with sacubitril/valsartan, depending on background ACEI/ARB dose. The most common reason for ineligibility is a low natriuretic peptide level. Keywords Heart failure Eligibility Sacubitril-valsartan Real-world population PARADIGM-HF University of Glasgow issue-copyright-statement © Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2019 Introduction The angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI) sacubitril/valsartan combines an angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB) with a neprilysin inhibitor. The Prospective comparison of ARNI with ACEI to Determine Impact on Global Mortality and morbidity in Heart Failure trial (PARADIGM-HF) demonstrated the superiority of the sacubitril/valsartan (formerly known as LCZ696) over the angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEI) enalapril in patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HF-REF) [ 1 ]. In PARADIGM-HF, sacubitril/valsartan reduced the risk of the primary composite outcome of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization by 20%, each of the components of that endpoint by a similar amount and all-cause death by 16% [ 1 ]. As a result, international guidelines now recommend the use of sacubitril/valsartan as a preferred alternative to an ACEI or ARB [ 2 , 3 ]. How widely applicable sacubitril/valsartan treatment is in unselected patients with HF-REF is uncertain. We used the Swedish Heart Failure Registry (SwedeHF) to examine eligibility of patients for sacubitril/valsartan in an unselected nationwide cohort. We identified individuals fulfilling the main inclusion criteria for the PARADIGM-HF trial, i.e., ambulatory patients with persisting symptoms (NYHA class II–IV), low ejection fraction (EF) (< 40%), and elevated natriuretic peptides, despite treatment with an ACEI or an ARB (scenario 1). To be enrolled in the PARADIGM-HF active run-in phase, patients had to be treated with a dose of ACE inhibitor or ARB equivalent to enalapril 10 mg daily—we further identified the subset of patients in SwedeHF treated in this way (scenario 2). Finally, as patients had to tolerate up-titration to a daily dose of 20 mg enalapril during the active run in, we also identified the proportion of patients in SwedeHF taking a dose of ACE inhibitor or ARB equivalent to this dose of enalapril (scenario 3). Methods Patients Patients with heart failure included in SwedeHF between July 2005 and December 2012 were studied. This nationwide internet-based registry has been described in detail [ 4 ]. Patients are included in the registry based upon a clinical diagnosis of heart failure and registered at discharge from hospital or following an outpatient visit. Data on over 100 primary and derived variables are collected, including clinical findings, laboratory measurements, and medications. Left ventricular EF is reported in the registry as less than 30%, 30–39%, 40–49%, and 50% or greater. For this study, we included only patients with an EF < 40%, and only the most recent patient encounter was considered. Eligibility for Sacubitril/Valsartan The entry criteria for PARADIGM-HF were used to determine eligibility status for each patient [ 5 ]. Patients were considered potentially eligible and included in the denominator in this study if they were not hospitalized (because only ambulatory patients were included in PARADIGM-HF; potentially eligible patients in both an outpatient and inpatient setting are shown in Supplementary Table 1 ) and had symptoms (NYHA functional class II–IV) and a low EF (< 40%) and were prescribed an ACEI or an ARB at a dose equivalent to enalapril 10 mg daily. The dose equivalents for these analyses were defined PARADIGM-HF inclusion criteria [ 5 ]. In these patients, we evaluated further eligibility in relation to the main additional PARADIGM-HF inclusion criteria, i.e., plasma B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) ≥ 150 pg/ml (or N-terminal pro-BNP [NT-proBNP] ≥ 600 pg/ml) or, in patients hospitalized for HF in the preceding 12 months, BNP ≥ 100 pg/ml or NT-proBNP ≥ 400 pg/ml; and exclusion criteria, i.e., systolic blood pressure (SBP) < 100 mmHg, serum potassium concentration > 5.2 mmol/l, or an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 30 ml/min/1.73 m 2 . For the main analyses, we only included patients with complete data entries for these inclusion and exclusion criteria. In a consistency analysis, missing data were imputed by multivariate imputation using chained equations. The extent of missing data is shown in Table 2 of the Supplementary Appendix. Background ACE Inhibitor Dose In PARADIGM-HF, patients had to be treated with an ACE inhibitor or an ARB at a dose equivalent to enalapril 10 mg/day for at least 4 weeks before the screening visit and then entered an active run-in phase where they received open-label enalapril which was titrated to a dose of 10 mg bid over a period of 3 to 5 weeks. Patients tolerating enalapril 10 mg bid were then started on sacubitril/valsartan 49/51 mg bid, which, if tolerated, was increased to a dose of 97/103 mg bid after 1–2 weeks. If tolerated, sacubitril/valsartan 97/103 mg bid was continued for a further 2–4 weeks, at which point patients were randomized to enalapril 10 mg bid or sacubitril/valsartan 97/103 mg bid. At each step, during the two run-in periods, patients had to demonstrate satisfactory renal function and serum potassium concentration, as well as a systolic blood pressure before randomization of at least 95 mmHg and no symptoms of hypotension. For this reason, we did separate analyses of otherwise eligible patients depending on whether they were on a background ACE inhibitor/ARB dose equivalent to 10 mg daily and 20 mg daily. Ethical Considerations Establishment of SwedeHF, and the present analysis, was approved by a multisite ethics committee. Patients in Sweden are informed of the intent to include their data in the national registry and may choose to opt out of this. Statistical Analysis For baseline characteristics, categorical data are presented as numbers and percentages and parametric data as mean and standard deviation (medians and interquartile ranges are used for data that are not normally distributed). Continuous variables were modeled with linear regression and dichotomous variables were imputed via logistic regression. In sensitivity analyses to avoid bias from data not missing at random, multiple imputation was used to handle missing data. We considered a two-sided p value < 0.05 as significant. All analyses were conducted using Stata version 14.1 (StataCorp LP, College Station, Texas).

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the 'real-world' eligibility of unselected, symptomatic outpatients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HF-REF) for sacubitril/valsartan treatment, using criteria from the PARADIGM-HF trial. It found that 34-76% of these patients are eligible, with eligibility significantly influenced by background ACEI/ARB dosing. The most common reasons for ineligibility were low natriuretic peptide levels, followed by low blood pressure, renal dysfunction (low eGFR), and hyperkalemia, which collectively accounted for 20-30% of exclusions.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on evaluating patient eligibility for sacubitril/valsartan based on PARADIGM-HF trial criteria, considering different background ACEI/ARB doses. Patients were deemed potentially eligible if they were on an ACEI or ARB dose equivalent to at least 10 mg enalapril daily, with further consideration for tolerating up-titration to 20 mg enalapril daily during an active run-in phase. The study did not report specific sacubitril/valsartan doses but observed its comparative effect on renal impairment and hyperkalemia during follow-up against enalapril. Eligibility varied depending on these background ACEI/ARB dose thresholds.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) / N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher in eligible patients; lower levels lead to ineligibility.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Ineligibility thresholds were BNP < 150 pg/ml (or NT-proBNP < 600 pg/ml), or for patients hospitalized for HF in the preceding 12 months, BNP < 100 pg/ml (or NT-proBNP < 400 pg/ml). This was the most common reason for ineligibility, affecting 13.7% to 16.1% of patients depending on the background ACEI/ARB dose (e.g., 14.9% or 462 of 3099 patients in the ">=10mg enalapril equivalent group). Higher concentrations are associated with greater absolute risk reduction from sacubitril/valsartan treatment.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicates cardiac stress, strain, and ventricular dysfunction, serving as a biomarker for heart failure severity and risk.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Eligibility assessment for sacubitril/valsartan treatment in symptomatic HF-REF patients, adhering to PARADIGM-HF trial inclusion criteria, including different background ACEI/ARB dosing scenarios.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated natriuretic peptide levels are a critical criterion for eligibility; low levels are the most common reason for ineligibility, suggesting less severe heart failure or a different pathophysiology. Higher levels also indicate higher absolute risk, suggesting a greater benefit from sacubitril/valsartan.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) / Serum Creatinine
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Blood Serum (for creatinine, eGFR derived from it)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Renal Function / Calculated Rate / Metabolite Concentration

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower for ineligibility; higher for eligible patients; lower risk of impairment with sacubitril/valsartan.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: An eGFR < 30 ml/min/1.73 m2 was an exclusion criterion. Ineligibility due to low eGFR (or high creatinine) ranged from 0.8% (for highest ACEI/ARB dose group) to 3.6% (for any ACEI/ARB dose group). Eligible patients generally had higher eGFR and lower creatinine. Sacubitril/valsartan (ARNI) demonstrated a lower risk of renal impairment during follow-up compared to enalapril.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: eGFR measures kidney filtration capacity; creatinine is a waste product marker used to estimate eGFR, reflecting kidney function and waste removal.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Exclusion criteria for sacubitril/valsartan treatment in HF-REF patients, as per PARADIGM-HF trial. Also, comparison of sacubitril/valsartan vs. enalapril's impact on renal function during treatment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Low eGFR or high creatinine indicates impaired kidney function, which is a contraindication for sacubitril/valsartan due to potential drug accumulation. Sacubitril/valsartan may offer a protective effect against renal impairment compared to enalapril.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher levels lead to ineligibility; lower levels characterize eligible patients; lower risk of hyperkalemia with sacubitril/valsartan compared to enalapril.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A concentration > 5.2 mmol/l was an exclusion criterion. Ineligibility due to hyperkalemia was infrequent, ranging from 1.2% to 1.4% across different ACEI/ARB dose categories. Sacubitril/valsartan demonstrated a lower risk of hyperkalemia during follow-up compared to enalapril.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Maintains electrolyte balance, crucial for cardiac electrophysiology, nerve, and muscle cell function, particularly heart rhythm.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Exclusion criteria for sacubitril/valsartan treatment in HF-REF patients, as per PARADIGM-HF trial. Also, comparison of sacubitril/valsartan vs. enalapril's impact on hyperkalemia risk during treatment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: High serum potassium (hyperkalemia) is a contraindication for sacubitril/valsartan due to cardiotoxic risks. The observation that sacubitril/valsartan may reduce hyperkalemia risk compared to enalapril is a significant health indicator for patient management.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower levels lead to ineligibility; higher levels characterize eligible patients.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Exclusion thresholds were < 100 mmHg at screening, and requiring at least 95 mmHg during the active run-in phase and prior to randomization. Ineligibility due to low SBP ranged from 5.9% (in the ">=20 mg ACEI/ARB group) to 9.1% (in the any dose ACEI/ARB group).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Measures arterial pressure, serving as a key indicator of cardiac output, peripheral vascular resistance, and overall cardiovascular function and risk.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Exclusion criteria for sacubitril/valsartan treatment in HF-REF patients, as defined by the PARADIGM-HF trial, including tolerance during active run-in phases with varying background ACEI/ARB doses.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Low SBP (hypotension) is a significant exclusion criterion for sacubitril/valsartan treatment due to increased risk of adverse cardiovascular events or intolerance. Higher SBP is associated with eligibility.
